clue.text: At first, start to go slowly, then write hurriedly

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows it, start

parts.note: to crawl is to go very slowly

explanation.surface: Advice to begin a task gently and then dash off the writing in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' takes S from 'start'; 'then' just joins it to CRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrawl is to scribble carelessly, as when writing in haste.

clue.text: One in the field in court for hiding things

parts.note: cover is a cricket fielding position
to be up before a judge is to be in court

explanation.surface: A fielder appears in court accused of concealing evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: COVER is a fielding position in cricket, a bat-and-ball game; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealment, a deliberate act of keeping something secret.

clue.text: So is this a full list of names of those taking part?

definitions.text: So is this a full list of names of those taking part?

parts.words: So is this a full list of names of those taking part?
parts.note: read literally it suggests every name in the cast; it describes a show or team of celebrities

explanation.surface: A query about whether a programme lists everyone involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is reading the term literally as a list of every name, all of them stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a cast or team made up entirely of famous performers.

clue.text: One in the field stages display of impudence

parts.note: legs are stages of a journey or contest
lip is cheek or insolent talk

explanation.surface: A fielder puts on a show of cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG SLIP is a cricket fielding position close behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A close catching position in cricket, filled by a fielder.

clue.text: Remote possibility monarch's taken measure of resistance

indicators.note: a possibility is one of several ways things might turn out, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: HM stands for His or Her Majesty, a monarch

explanation.surface: A far-fetched chance that the king has been taken somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote possibility' reads as a phrase, but 'possibility' is the anagram signal working on REMOTE plus HM; 'taken' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that gauges electrical resistance, which is counted in ohms.

clue.text: See most of manor with stairs in semi-darkness

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word for manor is dropped

parts.note: a hall is a manor house
a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: Look at most of a manor house with its staircase in dim light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' and 'with' are links; 'most of' cuts HALL to HAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim light, as at dusk, is a state of partial darkness.

clue.text: Logical premiss considered by youngster over some time at school

indicators.note: over means written above, which in a down answer puts the first piece before the second

parts.note: a minor is a person under age
a school term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A young pupil ponders a logical proposition over a school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'considered by' is a link; in a down entry 'over' puts MINOR above TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: In a syllogism, the minor term is the subject of the conclusion, appearing in the minor premiss.

clue.text: He would have publicised row about personal credit

indicators.note: about means the word for row is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
own means personal, belonging to oneself
CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: A person who would have broadcast a quarrel over someone's own loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to mean a quarrel; it is TIER, a row of seats, placed about OWN + CR.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who called out public announcements in the streets.

clue.text: It could be characterised as leafy, or even bits of frond

definitions.text: It could be characterised as leafy, or even bits of frond

indicators.note: characterised as is read as given another character, so the letters change order
even bits of means the second and fourth letters of the word frond

explanation.surface: A plant described as having lots of foliage, or at least pieces of frond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characterised as' rearranges LEAFY OR into ROYALFE; 'even bits of' takes R and N from 'frond'. 'It could be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fern species whose leafy fronds make the whole clue a description of it.

clue.text: Grounds to take a test

parts.note: reads like reasons for sitting an exam, but means a cricket venue where a Test match is played

explanation.surface: Justification for sitting an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground that hosts Test matches; 'test' is the cricket kind, not an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Named for its shape, this south London ground is a regular venue for international Test cricket.

clue.text: Aim to have year on wagon, out to achieve lasting effect

parts.note: an aim is a goal

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A resolution to stay on the wagon, abstaining from drink, for a year so that it has a lasting effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges Y and WAGON into ONGWAY; 'to have' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something that goes a long way has a large or lasting effect.

clue.text: Fairy-tale character allowed bit of work, given backing

indicators.note: given backing tells us the whole string is turned to read from back to front

parts.note: to let is to allow
the erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A storybook figure was permitted a small task and some support.
explanation.walkthrough: The erg is the old CGS unit of work, a crossword favourite for 'bit of work'; 'given backing' turns the whole charade round.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl who, with her brother Hansel, outwits the witch in the Grimm story.

clue.text: Maybe vicar's working in an office

definitions.meaning: belonging to a member of the clergy, a vicar being one example
describing office work such as filing and typing

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both relating to clergy and relating to office clerks.

clue.text: Does it, help to start driving swallows back round garden?

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes around the word for garden
back tells us the word for swallows is read backwards

parts.note: gulps means swallows
a park is a public garden

explanation.surface: A question about whether a motorist gulping something back while circling a park helps get them going.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has no comma: 'Does it' is a link, and 'back' reverses the swallowing word before 'round' wraps it about the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The device that sparks the fuel in an engine, needed before a car can be driven.

clue.text: Temporarily stopped, having a hang-up?

definitions.meaning: halted for a time, as a match or payment
literally hung up, dangling from something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both halted for a period and hung from a support.

clue.text: Declares girl's put on some weight?

indicators.note: put on means placed on top of, which in a down entry puts this name first

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
ounces are units of weight

explanation.surface: A young woman has gained a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' looks like gaining weight, but it places ANN above OUNCES.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to proclaim or declare publicly.

clue.text: Native of Australia in great difficulty using colloquialism?

definitions.text: Native of Australia in great difficulty using colloquialism?

parts.words: Native of Australia in great difficulty using colloquialism?
parts.note: an Australian marsupial whose popular name wrongly calls it a bear, as in the slang that a hard thing is a bear

explanation.surface: An Australian struggles badly when speaking in slang.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is a marsupial, not a bear, so 'bear' in its name is only colloquial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-dwelling marsupial native to Australia, popularly but wrongly called a bear.

clue.text: Cash needed to dress up as Roman poet

parts.note: lucre is money, cash

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a suit is an outfit, something to dress in

explanation.surface: Money is needed to dress up as a poet of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress up' looks like a phrase; 'up' turns SUIT over; 'needed to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of De Rerum Natura, a philosophical poem of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Once, for Napoleon, island implied this

definitions.text: Once, for Napoleon, island implied this

parts.note: ex means former, once
île is French for island, the word Napoleon would use

explanation.surface: Napoleon's islands, Elba and St Helena, carried a meaning for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was banished to Elba and later St Helena, so for him an island meant banishment: the wordplay and the definition are the same words.
explanation.definitionFit: Banishment from one's homeland, which Napoleon twice suffered on islands.

clue.text: Champion driver once given help to get in motion?

definitions.meaning: Ayrton ..., the Brazilian Formula One world champion who died in 1994
a laxative that helps produce a bowel motion

explanation.definitionFit: The racing driver's surname, and a plant extract used as a laxative.

clue.text: Boat by a river can put about

indicators.note: put about means placed around, so the word for can surrounds the rest

parts.note: taken as written
the Tamar is a river dividing Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: A vessel moored beside a river where a tin can is tossed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put about' sounds nautical, but it means placed around; 'by' joins the river to A. The Tamar is the river between Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin-hulled sailing vessel is a type of boat.

clue.text: Lazy at heart -in another case, completely in a state

definitions.text: Lazy at heart -in another case, completely in a state

parts.words: Lazy at heart -in another case, completely in a state
parts.note: the middle letters of lazy, written in capitals, form a US postal code; spelt out in full they name the state it stands for

explanation.surface: Someone idle deep down, and in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of 'lazy' is az; in upper case that is AZ, the US state abbreviation, and written completely it is the state's full name. 'in a state' looks like agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A south-western US state whose postal abbreviation is AZ.

clue.text: Sailor almost overwhelmed by excited "Ciao! in island port

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the shortened sailor is engulfed inside the jumbled letters
excited means stirred up, so the letters of the greeting are jumbled
almost means the last letter of the word for sailor is dropped

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is swamped by an enthusiastic farewell in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges the Italian greeting, and the result swallows the clipped sailor; Ajaccio is on Corsica.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital and chief port of Corsica, Napoleon's birthplace.

clue.text: Places where bass could be seen as really getting into solo

definitions.text: Places where bass could be seen

indicators.note: getting into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
qua is Latin for as, in the sense of in the capacity of

explanation.surface: Somewhere a bass singer could really shine is in a solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bass' is the fish, not the singer, which the solo encourages you to think of.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanks where fish are kept on display; a bass is a fish.

clue.text: Well up in class system

parts.note: reads like being high in the social order, but means knowledgeable as a result of schooling in classes

explanation.surface: Someone sitting high in the social hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' looks social, but it means school classes; 'well up' means knowledgeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone schooled and knowledgeable, the product of a system of lessons.

clue.text: Fantastic winger brought down in the heat of the moment

definitions.text: Fantastic winger brought down in the heat of the moment

parts.words: Fantastic winger brought down in the heat of the moment
parts.note: reads like a footballer fouled in a rash moment, but means a mythical flyer whose wax wings melted near the sun

explanation.surface: A brilliant wide player is tackled in a moment of rashness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests football; 'Fantastic' means from fantasy, and the heat is the sun's.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the son of Daedalus flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell into the sea.

clue.text: Enhance reputation of medic concerning the aforesaid

parts.note: doc is short for doctor, a medic
re means concerning
ditto means the same as said before

explanation.surface: Something improves a doctor's standing regarding what was mentioned earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to bring honour to someone, raising their standing.

clue.text: Trite jokes falling on deaf ears?

definitions.text: Trite jokes falling on deaf ears?

parts.words: Trite jokes falling on deaf ears?
parts.note: stale humour that nobody laughs at, and also a crop whose ears cannot hear

explanation.surface: Hackneyed gags that get no response from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant's ears are deaf because they are seed heads, not organs of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Corny humour is stale, and the cereal crop carries ears that hear nothing.

clue.text: Doubt lack of confidence

definitions.meaning: a verb, to be suspicious of
a noun, an absence of faith in someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a verb meaning to suspect and a noun meaning want of faith.

clue.text: Jacket brought in to clean, or a kaftan?

indicators.note: brought in says the letters sit inside the words clean, or a kaftan, running across them

explanation.surface: A coat is taken to the dry cleaner's, or is it really a kaftan?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the run spans 'cleAN OR A Kaftan'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded waterproof jacket.
